commands: kubectl get pods -n test-social-network; kubectl get events -n test-social-network --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -20

cd /tmp; kubectl get svc,ep -n test-social-network | awk '{print $1,$2,$3,$4,$5}' | head -70; for p in $(kubectl get deploy -n test-social-network -o name); do echo $p; kubectl get $p -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].ports[*].containerPort}{"\n"}'; done
kubectl get svc user-service media-frontend -n test-social-network -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.spec.ports}{"\n"}{end}'
kubectl patch svc user-service -n test-social-network --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":9090}]'; kubectl get ep user-service -n test-social-network
agent.summary:
I found one fault and fixed it: the `user-service` Service had `targetPort: 9999`, but the pod listens on 9090. Traffic to it was going to a closed port, so anything that calls user-service (register/login, for example) would have failed.

I changed the Service's `targetPort` to 9090. Its endpoint now shows `10.244.1.84:9090`.

All pods were Running with no restarts, and every other Service pointed at the right port. I didn't run an end-to-end request after the patch.

`media-frontend` maps port 8081 to 8080 while its container declares 8081. I left it alone because that mapping looks like the stock configuration.
